newsitem.title: USA: LOT AIRLINES EX-JFK EXPORTS UP 62 PCT.
newsitem.headline: LOT AIRLINES EX-JFK EXPORTS UP 62 PCT.

text.p: Lot Polish Airlines handled 175 tonnes of outbound commercial freight at John F. Kennedy airport in July, up 62 percent from 108 tonnes in same 1996 month, Margaret Budnica, cargo sales manager for the carrier's JFK station, told Reuters.
The carrier handled 131 tonnes of inbound cargo, down two percent from 134 tonnes in July 1996, she said.
The sharp increase of cargo tonnage exported from JFK in July was primarily due to the rate adjustments the carrier implemented in the beginning of the Summer, Budnicka said.
The rates were down at least 60 percent from year-earlier levels and these reductions have prompted additional agents to work with the carrier, she added.
Lot Polish operated 31 flights between New York and Poland in July, the same as in July 1996.

Budnica said electronics, machinery and medical equipment headed the carrier's outbound list of commodities in July while apparel, unfinished textile, and newspapers topped its imported commodity list. In July 1996, it handled the same commodities. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
